![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064036/assets/7456b549ac815ab491945d9b3f2873d65b091636f7b8282f296a435954ba503d.png)

Find the volume of the solid region above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the right one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064036/assets/702e54d6f4b951eec56a62d340f81df1f618622114cfef6045460a6d184bffbc.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type III region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le 3-x-z},
$$

where

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064036/assets/af505b53a12bbe74da4d3885df59c4c00cc7bfaf71df9f7167caa9dbf67cfb73.png)

Hence, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 3-x-z}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3-x-z}dy\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[y]_{y=0}^{y=3-x-z}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(3-x-z)-0\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}3-x-z\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[(3-x)z-\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}((3-x)(1)-\frac{{1}^{2}}{2})-0\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{5}{2}-x\,dx \\  & ={[\frac{5}{2}x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =(\frac{5}{2}(1)-\frac{{1}^{2}}{2})-0 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
